posts.title: Before It's Lost — Rebuilding the Sega Saturn's development environment on a modern PC
posts.description: CartDev, SEGA's official Saturn development cartridge, was becoming unusable — not because it broke, but because the DOS-and-SCSI world around it did. I captured the USB traffic, disassembled the on-target monitor to decode the protocol, and rebuilt a way to load, run and debug programs on real Saturn hardware straight from a modern PC, with no DOS and no virtual machine in between.

posts.title: Rebuilding VDP2 — Reproducing the Saturn’s “read-and-composite” pipeline per pixel, in real-hardware order
posts.description: I rebuilt the emulation of the Sega Saturn’s background processor, VDP2, from scratch. A new compositor fetches each pixel by priority on a per-scanline basis and runs color calculation in the exact order the real hardware does — fixing Doom’s see-through walls, Azel’s translucent menus, Luna’s tinted text, and more.

posts.title: YabaSanshiro's VDP1 rendering gets even more accurate — reproducing SEGA Saturn drawing with Compute Shaders
posts.description: YabaSanshiro is an emulator that actively leverages the GPU so that SEGA Saturn games run comfortably on modern hardware.
